subject: Pilot pricing & technical ask — autoscale credits, quantization impact and cache guidance

Subject: Pilot ask: credits + autoscale behavior + quantization impact

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudWave is keen to run a 6-week pilot (external-facing search augmentation) to validate latency at scale and compare unit costs across a few model variants. Before we lock dates, can you confirm:

- Pilot pricing options: credits vs small committed pool — we have to present a clear cost comparison to our CFO.
- How autoscale interacts with credits: if we exceed the pilot credit bucket, do requests fall back to a higher-latency queued path or to a pay-as-you-go rate?
- Any recommended quantization profiles you’d advise for a 4k-context LLaMA-family model vs an LLM-2 style model — we’re sensitive about NLG quality on prompts with long context.
- Does KV caching behave across autoscaled nodes or is it per-instance (we have many short-lived sessions)?

We attached our rough throughput estimates and typical prompt length distribution. Can you share a short commercial proposal and the technical constraints we should know about?

Elena
Elena Rossi

CloudWave

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet — that helped. High level answers and a next-step proposal below. I’m attaching a short pricing sketch (RW-Optimize-pilot-credit-model-v2.pdf).

1) Pricing options (pilot-friendly):
  - Credits model: X credits = 500k token-equivalent. Useful if you want no upfront commitment; we issue credits that consume first and then fall back to PAYG.
  - Mini-commit (reserved burst pool): small monthly commit with autoscale buffer. Starts cheaper per-token once committed.

2) Autoscale + credits behavior:
  - Credits are consumed first by route. If credits are exhausted, autoscale still spins up capacity but requests are billed PAYG. We do not queue requests at the API layer; we prefer predictable routing and will surface rate-limit or capacity errors if your concurrency exceeds the configured SLOs.

3) KV caching across autoscaled nodes:
  - Default: KV cache is per-instance. For short-lived sessions we recommend sticky routing or a shared Redis-backed prefix cache (we can stand up a managed prefix cache for the pilot). That tends to preserve latency gains for repeated prefixes.

4) Quantization recommendations:
  - For LLaMA-family 4k: float16 or int8 quant with per-channel calibration is a reasonable starting point; preserves quality and reduces memory pressure.
  - For LLM-2 style: prefer int8-pp or q4_x4 for inference; run sample evals — small BLEU/ROUGE/LLM evals we can run for you.

Next steps I propose:
  - 1-hour workshop (tech + commercial) this week to align on throughput SLOs and pick the pilot model variants.
  - We’ll provide two pilot commercial options (credits + mini-commit) and an expected spend envelope per 100k active users.

@Karthik / @Grace — can you add a short technical note on fallback model variants (latency/quality tradeoffs) and a recommended concession band for a 6-week proof?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Elena — quick technical note from infra/serving perspective. TL;DR: choices depend on your throughput vs. latency tradeoff.

- Quantization: for LLaMA-4k-context, start with int8 + per-channel calibration. It reduces GPU memory by ~35-45% and keeps generation quality near fp16 for most prompt classes. For critical prompts with long provenance, run a 100-sample head-to-head eval (we’ll do this in the workshop).

- Fallback model variants: pick a lower-capacity variant (e.g., 13B quantized) as the first fallback. That gives ~30–40% latency reduction at small quality cost; we can configure per-route fallback thresholds (latency > 250ms triggers fallback).

- KV cache/Shared prefix cache: our runtime supports a managed prefix cache option. For pilots with many short sessions, shared cache + sticky routing increases hit rate and reduces token compute by up to 20% in our benchmarks. Note this requires a small additional infra charge (we can include that in the pilot credits).

I’ll prepare a one-page tech appendix to attach to the commercial sketch.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Elena — commercial follow-up from my side. Two pilot structures we usually propose for customers at your scale:

Option A — Credits-first pilot (minimal legal overhead)
  - Commitment: one-time purchase of pilot credits equivalent to ~$12k-$20k spend depending on model selection.
  - Concession: 10% invoice-credit if you roll to a 6-12 month committed plan within 60 days.
  - Pros: fast to start, limited contract work.

Option B — Mini-commit + autoscale buffer (preferred for predictable demos)
  - Commitment: small monthly reserved capacity (e.g., 4 reserved vGPUs), plus a 20% autoscale buffer billed PAYG beyond commit.
  - Concession: volume discount tiering: 5% at 3 months commit, 10% at 6 months. For pilot we can offer a 15% pilot goodwill discount on the reserved portion.
  - Pros: lower per-token cost during steady-state; clearer CFO reporting.

Additional notes:
  - We can include the managed prefix cache as part of the pilot credits at a nominal $500 setup fee.
  - SOC2 evidence and a standard DPA addendum are available; legal can push a simple SOW for pilots.

Elena — if you send target spend range and whether you prefer a quick start vs a CFO-friendly commit, I’ll draft both commercial options into the SOW.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
